THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 10.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA. No.111/2018  3  2025:KER:11430  JUDGMENT
Dated this the 10th day of February, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.976/2011 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kollam is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 19.1.2010.

According to the petitioner, on 19.1.2010 at about 5.30 p.m., while he was trying to cross the road at Moonamkutti on Kollam-Schencotta National Highway, he was hit down by a motor cycle bearing registration No.KL-4V-3867 ridden by the 2 nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner and as a result of which, the petitioner fell down and sustained serious injuries.

sentences.text: The 1st respondent is the owner , the 2 nd respondent is the rider and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the 2025:KER:11430 offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.12,00,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence Exts.A1 toA11.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,60,195/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri Pratheesh P, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Smt.P.A.
Reziya P.A, represented by Smt. K.S. Santhi , the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.

According to him, the petitioner was working as fisherman,
earning Rs.10,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.4,000/-.

The learned counsel would argue that the notional income of a coolie during the year 2010 will come to Rs.7500/-, in the light of the decision of the Hon'be Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236] and as such the notional income of the petitioner could not be fixed below that of a coolie.

entities.text:
Ramachandrappa v.
Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

11. As rightly argued by the learned counsel, in the light of the the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2011 will come to Rs.7500/-
and as such the notional income of the petitioner could not be fixed below that of a coolie.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the notional income of 2025:KER:11430 the petitioner is fixed at Rs.7500/-.

sentences.text:
In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"1. Lacerated wound on tight tibia with bone exposed.
2. Lacerated wound on right occipital region of scalp 3. fracture right tibia 4. Fracture both bone of right leg."
13.
As per Exhibit A6 disability certificate the petitioner sustained fracture tibia right, Type II open both bone fracture, right leg along with FTP SDH along with haemotoma,
It further shows that 2.25 mm FTP and 18.8 mm MDH.
The petitioner was treated with evacuation, (bone flap kept in refrigerator).
The treatment certificate also shows that the petitioner was initially treated at the ventilator.
He was treated as inpatient for a total period of 11 days.

14. After examining the petitioner-in-person, the tribunal observed in the Award that that:
"12.
........ ....... ........ The petitioner was present before the court.
On examination it can be found out that his both hands could not move.
Left side head-scalp completely damaged and he could not walk without the help of another person.
Left side temporal parietal bone got damaged.
No doubt being a man of 2025:KER:11430 aged 36 years, he completely and permanently got disabled.

So on a clear analysis of materials on record, I am of the view that the disability can be fixed at 50%."
15.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that because of the injuries sustained in the accident, both the hands of the petitioner became paralysed.
He is unable to do any job, especially he was a fisherman by profession.

On a perusal of the observation made by the Tribunal in the impugned Award that both the hands of the petitioner could not be moved, it is evident that the petitioner could not continue his profession as a fisherman and as such he is unable to do any job or earn anything for his livelihood.
Therefore, his functional disability is liable to be fixed at 100%.
16. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 36 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 15, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded Rs.40,000/- being the income for 10 months @Rs.4,000/- .

Since the functional disability of the petitioner is re-fixed at 100%, he is not entitled to get any further compelling on the head 'loss of earning'.

Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded only Rs.30,000/- and towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.1,20,000/- was awarded.

Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the percentage of disability suffered by him, I hold that the compensation awarded on the head 'pain and suffering', 'loss of amenities of life' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.3,00,000/- each.
19.
Since the Tribunal has noticed that the petitioner could not walk without the help of another person, he is also entitled to get the expense of a bystander.
In the decision in Kajal v. Jagadish Chand and Others, AIR 2020 SC 776= [(2020) 4 SCC 413] the Hon'ble Supreme Court has fixed the expense of a bystander at Rs.5,000/- per month.

(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%).
